records.text: Paper card. System: W-containing refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs). Processing: various techniques, including vacuum arc melting (VAM), powder metallurgy, mechanical alloying (MA), gas atomization, magnetron sputtering (MS), and additive manufacturing (AM). Test conditions: room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 1600 ℃). Findings: W-containing RHEAs have high hardness and melting points; excellent mechanical properties at high temperatures; single-phase BCC structures are generally strong but brittle; multi-phase RHEAs can have improved strength and plasticity; yield strength of W-containing RHEAs can exceed 1000 MPa; plasticity of W-containing RHEAs can be improved by optimizing composition and processing techniques. Mechanism: high-mixing entropy, sluggish diffusion effect, lattice distortion effect, and cocktail effect. Limitations: room-temperature brittleness, high density, and limited plasticity. Future work: optimization of composition and processing techniques to improve mechanical properties, investigation of deformation and strengthening mechanisms at high temperatures. Quote: "the Gibbs free energy of the HEA system can be significantly reduced"

item.research_question: How do W-containing refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties and neutron irradiation resistance under extreme conditions?
item.material_system: W-containing RHEAs, such as VCrFeTaxWx (x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 1), MoWAlCrTi, TixWTaVCr, and W0.5(TaTiVCr)0.5
item.processing_route: Vacuum arc melting (VAM), mechanical alloying (MA), spark plasma sintering (SPS), and magnetron sputtering (MS)
item.test_conditions: High temperatures (up to 1200 °C), neutron irradiation, and corrosive environments (such as sulfuric acid and NaCl solution)
key_findings: The VCrFeTa0.1W0.1 and VCrFeTa0.2W0.2 RHEAs demonstrated improved hardness and exhibited a compressive yield strength exceeding 1000 MPa after annealing at 600 and 800 °C
The MoWAlCrTi RHEA showed excellent high-temperature oxidation resistance, with a specific mass change of only about 0.2 mg/(cm2·h) after exposure to air at 1000 °C for 40 h
The W0.5(TaTiVCr)0.5 RHEA exhibited excellent irradiation resistance, with only slight damage after He+ ion irradiation
The WNbMoTaV RHEA showed superior wear resistance, with a wear rate almost 80% lower than Inconel 718 using an Al ball under a 2000 m sliding distance
item.mechanism: The excellent functional properties of W-containing RHEAs are attributed to the formation of dense oxide protective layers, passive films, and solid solution strengthening
item.limitations: The number of reported W-containing RHEAs is far less than the theoretically predicted systems, and the effects of different elements on the phase structure, mechanical properties, and functional characteristics of RHEAs are not fully understood
item.future_work: Further research is necessary to develop new W-containing RHEA systems with high-end properties, to reveal the strengthening and deformation mechanisms of W-containing RHEAs in harsh environments, and to investigate the machining performance of W-containing RHEAs
quotes: excellent mechanical properties and stability at high temperatures

records.text: Paper card. Question: How do W-containing refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) exhibit excellent mechanical properties and neutron irradiation resistance under extreme conditions?. System: W-containing RHEAs, such as VCrFeTaxWx (x = 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4 and 1), MoWAlCrTi, TixWTaVCr, and W0.5(TaTiVCr)0.5. Processing: Vacuum arc melting (VAM), mechanical alloying (MA), spark plasma sintering (SPS), and magnetron sputtering (MS). Test conditions: High temperatures (up to 1200 °C), neutron irradiation, and corrosive environments (such as sulfuric acid and NaCl solution). Findings: The VCrFeTa0.1W0.1 and VCrFeTa0.2W0.2 RHEAs demonstrated improved hardness and exhibited a compressive yield strength exceeding 1000 MPa after annealing at 600 and 800 °C; The MoWAlCrTi RHEA showed excellent high-temperature oxidation resistance, with a specific mass change of only about 0.2 mg/(cm2·h) after exposure to air at 1000 °C for 40 h; The W0.5(TaTiVCr)0.5 RHEA exhibited excellent irradiation resistance, with only slight damage after He+ ion irradiation; The WNbMoTaV RHEA showed superior wear resistance, with a wear rate almost 80% lower than Inconel 718 using an Al ball under a 2000 m sliding distance. Mechanism: The excellent functional properties of W-containing RHEAs are attributed to the formation of dense oxide protective layers, passive films, and solid solution strengthening. Limitations: The number of reported W-containing RHEAs is far less than the theoretically predicted systems, and the effects of different elements on the phase structure, mechanical properties, and functional characteristics of RHEAs are not fully understood. Future work: Further research is necessary to develop new W-containing RHEA systems with high-end properties, to reveal the strengthening and deformation mechanisms of W-containing RHEAs in harsh environments, and to investigate the machining performance of W-containing RHEAs. Quote: "excellent mechanical properties and stability at high temperatures"
